title: Add per-token tail-latency fingerprinting and alert deduplication
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Introduce token-tail-latency fingerprint metric and alert dedup engine to reduce noise from long-tail token outliers; dashboard panels and alert rules updated; rollout gated behind FF=token_tail_fp.
description:
Context and motivation:
We saw an increasing number of noisy P95/P99 alerts driven by rare per-token latency spikes (long-tail tokens) coming from a small fraction of requests. Existing per-route histograms and token-cost breakdowns surface the symptom but not an actionable signal that groups repeated, similar spikes. This PR adds a lightweight per-token tail-latency fingerprint and a deduplication layer for alert rules so we can consolidate repeated long-tail incidents into a single actionable alert and reduce pager fatigue.

What this changes (high level):
- New metric: telemetry.token_tail_fingerprint (labelled by model, token_hash, hardware_arch, region, route). The metric is an event counter emitted when an observed per-token latency exceeds an adaptive threshold (computed via exp-decay baseline per model+route).
- Derived rollups: telemetry.token_tail_p95_ms and telemetry.token_tail_unique_fingerprints (daily).
- Tracing change: span enrichment adds token-window signature fields (last-8 token hashes) when the per-token latency sampler flags a tail event. This is gated behind feature-flag: token_tail_fp=true.
- Alert dedup engine: new job in observability service that consumes fingerprint events, clusters similar fingerprints using a cheap locality-preserving hash, and presents a consolidated alert context (first-seen, count, sample span id). Grafana alert rules updated to call the dedup endpoint instead of raw counters.
- Dashboards: new panels in "Inference / Token Tail Insights" showing top fingerprints, their sample spans, and host/region distribution.
- Rollout: gradual rollout via FF, opt-in to Dedicated tenants for first 48 hours, and automatic rollback on increased alert saturation.

Implementation notes and rationale:
- Fingerprint design uses a 64-bit XXHash over compacted token IDs + a small token-position mask; collision probability is low and acceptable given that dedup is advisory (we still include raw span ids for triage).
- Thresholding uses an exponential moving median per model/route with a timescale tuned for production traffic (alpha=0.025). This prevents one-off bursts from permanently inflating thresholds.
- The dedup job maintains a short in-memory LRU of recent fingerprints (TTL 24h) and writes aggregated fingerprints to the telemetry DB for downstream dashboards and attribution.
- Kept the tracer change minimal: only attach token-window signature when an event is flagged to avoid high-cardinality tag explosion.

Files changed (high level):
- services/observability/fingerprint/processor.go: new dedup job and ingestion pipeline (adds most logic).
- services/observability/api/routes.go: new endpoints /v1/fingerprints/summary and /v1/fingerprints/samples.
- runtime/tracer/token_sampler.go: per-token tail sampler, emits event to obs pipeline when flagged.
- metrics/definitions.yaml: new metric definitions and alert query templates.
- grafana/dashboards/token_tail_insights.json: dashboard JSON with panels and alert links.
- telemetry/migrations/20260301_add_token_fingerprint.sql: schema additions for fingerprint rollups.
- sdk/python/redwood/tracing.py: small opt-in helper to include token-window when FF is enabled.
- docs/observability/token_tail_fingerprinting.md: implementation and operator guide.

Commits (summary):
- add processor skeleton and ingest path
- implement XXHash-based fingerprint and clustering logic
- add EM-median thresholding and sampler integration
- export metrics and update metrics spec + dashboard
- add unit tests and integration harness for dedup job
- docs + rollout FF + smoke tests

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for fingerprint collision bounds and clustering heuristics (added to services/observability/fingerprint/*_test.go).
- Integration test in perf-canary that triggers synthetic long-tail tokens and validates a single consolidated alert is produced.
- Local e2e run against staging observability stack validated dashboards render and sample span links resolve.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Priya Shah: "Can we quantify collision risk and add a CI test that asserts collision rate < 1e-6 for realistic token distributions?"
  - Asha: "Added a statistical unit test with seeds and documented the assumptions in the design notes (see fingerprint/collision_test.go)."
- Diego Alvarez: "Alert dedup may hide multi-host correlated issues. Ensure dedup exposes host distribution in the alert context."
  - Asha: "Dedup summary now returns host/region histogram and top-3 sample spans. Verified in integration run."
- Evan Kim: "Tracer change looks safe but we need FF and opt-in for Dedicated tenants during rollout."
  - Asha: "Feature flag added; Dedicated tenants are excluded by default for initial 48h canary."
- Diego (follow-up): "Can the processor OOM under high cardinality?"
  - Asha: "Processor uses size-bounded LRU + backpressure (drop on overflow) and metrics for drops; documented tradeoffs in the operator guide."

CI summary and iterations:
- Initial run: unit tests failed due to an off-by-one in token-window serialization (fixed in commit 3).
- Second run: integration flaky on perf-canary (race in in-memory dedup TTL). Added synchronization and re-ran.
- Final run: all checks green. Key checks: unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, lint: pass, perf-canary: pass (synthetic), e2e-staging: pass.

Migration and operational notes:
- telemetry DB migration adds a small fingerprint table; roll-forward is backwards-compatible (no writes until FF enabled).
- Operators should monitor telemetry.fingerprint_ingest_drops and telemetry.fingerprint_cluster_latency during rollout.
- If rollouts increase alert saturation unexpectedly, FF can be toggled off and dedup ingestion will stop producing events.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: deploy feature flag defaults to off in prod, enable for 3 internal canary orgs for 48h.
- Week 1: enable for 25% of traffic in hosted API and a few Dedicated tenants (opt-in).
- Week 2: GA if no regression in alert volume or CPU/billing impact.

Merge outcome:
- Merged by: Diego Alvarez via squash merge on 2026-03-02 after two approvals.

Notes for future work:
- Consider probabilistic fingerprint downsampling to further reduce ingest rate for very high-volume models.
- Add automatic suggested remediation in alerts (e.g., model-quantization hints) if a fingerprint correlates with specific model versions.

References:
- Linear ENG-4123 (token tail alert reduction)
- Internal incident INT-9345 (noisy token P99 alerts, Nov 2025)

Checklist (completed):
- [x] Design doc reviewed
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Dashboards + alerts updated
- [x] Docs and operator guide
- [x] Feature flag and rollout configured

This change is intentionally conservative in data cardinality and provides operator-visible controls; intent is to reduce long-tail alert noise while preserving triage fidelity.
